title: Enhancing Cas9 Efficiency and Fidelity through Phosphate-Locking Loop Engineering
author: Yang, Chen, et al.
materials: NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina
N1102 corresponds to FrCas9 V1103.ii.For GsCas

steps.title: Identify PLL motif via alignment
steps.instruction: Perform sequence alignment and structural cavity analysis to locate the phosphate‑locking loop (PLL) motif and assess engineering feasibility.

substeps.instruction: Obtain Cas9 protein sequences of the target ortholog and reference sequences (FrCas9 D1101‑S1102‑V1103 and SpCas9 K1107‑E1108‑S1109) from UniProt or NCBI.
Run a multiple‑sequence alignment with Clustal Omega or MUSCLE using default global‑alignment parameters; export the alignment in Clustal format.
Locate the region aligning to FrCas9 residues 1095‑1110, identify the three‑residue PLL motif, and record the residue numbers and native amino acids at these positions in the target Cas9.
Evaluate conservation of the PLL region: >60 % identity = high reliability; 40‑60 % = moderate (recommend additional structural validation); <40 % = low (consider alternative positions).

Assess cavity size at the target position: for FrCas9 V1103 the cavity is ~63 Å³ (surface area 133 Å²). Use the following guidelines – >50 Å³ can accommodate K or R; 30‑50 Å³ may fit smaller residues (N, Q); <30 Å³ is challenging.
Visualize the target residue and surrounding amino acids (5 Å radius) in ChimeraX v1.4, display the DNA backbone, and note any steric constraints from neighboring residues.
Document cavity geometry with annotated images for reference.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Prepare HEK293T cells and deliver Cas9‑variant and sgRNA plasmids by liposomal transfection to assess on‑target editing.

substeps.instruction: Culture HEK293T cells in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; keep passages between 5‑15 and maintain logarithmic growth.
Seed 1 × 10⁵ cells per well in a 24‑well plate one day before transfection; aim for 70‑80 % confluency on transfection day.
Prepare DNA mixture per well: 500 ng Cas9‑variant plasmid + 500 ng sgRNA plasmid in 50 µL Opti‑MEM.
In a separate tube, mix 2 µL Hieff Trans® Liposomal Transfection Reagent (Yeasen) with 50 µL Opti‑MEM, vortex 15 s, and incubate at 25 °C for 5 min.
Add the diluted transfection reagent to the DNA mixture dropwise while gently mixing; incubate at 25 °C for 15‑20 min to form complexes.
Add the DNA‑lipid complexes dropwise to the cells, rock the plate gently for even distribution, and optionally monitor morphology at 6‑8 h.
If cellular stress is observed (rounding, >10 % detachment, vacuolization), replace medium with 500 µL fresh complete medium.
Incubate transfected cells for 72 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, monitoring health daily.
Harvest cells, wash once with PBS, and extract genomic DNA using the TIANcombi DNA Lyse&Det PCR Kit (Tiangen) per the manufacturer’s protocol.
Quantify DNA on a NanoDrop (A260/A280 = 1.8‑2.0) and adjust to 50‑100 ng/µL for downstream PCR; store DNA at –20 °C (short‑term) or –80 °C (long‑term).
Include wild‑type Cas9, empty vector, and untransfected controls in every experiment.

steps.title: Electroporate cells for GUIDE‑seq
steps.instruction: Introduce Cas9‑variant plasmid, sgRNA plasmid, and dsODN tag into HEK293T cells by nucleofection for off‑target detection.

substeps.instruction: Expand HEK293T cells to obtain ≥5 × 10⁶ cells per condition; keep cells at 70‑80 % confluency and passages 5‑15.
Trypsinize, count, and wash cells twice with PBS.
Resuspend cell pellet in SF Nucleofector solution (Lonza SF Cell Line 4D‑Nucleofector X Kit, Cat# V4XC‑2024) at 2 × 10⁷ cells/mL.
Prepare electroporation mix per reaction: 2 × 10⁵ cells (10 µL), 2 µg Cas9‑variant plasmid, 2 µg sgRNA plasmid, 200 pmol dsODN tag, in SF solution.
Transfer the mixture to a Nucleocuvette strip (avoid bubbles) and electroporate using the 4D‑Nucleofector X Unit with program CM‑130 (or the manufacturer‑recommended program for HEK293T).
Immediately add 500 µL pre‑warmed DMEM (37 °C) to each well of a 24‑well plate; avoid cold medium.
Culture cells for 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ (optimal for GUIDE‑seq tag integration).
At 24 h, verify recovery: ≥70 % attachment and normal morphology; poor recovery may indicate suboptimal electroporation.
Harvest cells by trypsinization, wash with PBS, and extract genomic DNA using a high‑quality kit.
Run 0.8 % agarose gel: load 200‑500 ng DNA per lane, run at 100 V for 30‑40 min, and confirm a single high‑molecular‑weight band (>10 kb) with minimal smearing.
Quantify DNA on a NanoDrop (A260/A280 ≈ 1.8) and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of editing data
steps.instruction: Compile on‑target amplicon‑seq results, calculate relative activities, and test significance.

substeps.instruction: Gather editing efficiencies for each Cas9 variant across all screened target sites (minimum three sites, n ≥ 3 biological replicates).
Compute mean efficiency and standard error (SEM) for each variant.
Normalize to wild‑type Cas9 at the same site: relative activity (%) = (variant / WT) × 100.
Perform one‑way ANOVA comparing all variants to wild‑type, followed by Dunnett’s post‑hoc test for pairwise comparisons.
Apply Benjamini‑Hochberg correction (FDR < 0.05) to control false discoveries.

steps.title: Rank and select optimal variants
steps.instruction: Prioritize variants based on activity, structural criteria, and off‑target profiles to identify the lead PLL engineering candidate.

substeps.instruction: Rank variants by average on‑target activity across the initial three sites.
Select variants with ≥110 % relative activity versus wild‑type.
Prioritize positively charged, linear side‑chain substitutions (K, R) as indicated by the FrCas9 V1103K/R results.
Exclude aromatic (F, Y, W), negatively charged (D, E), and proline substitutions.
Compare GUIDE‑seq off‑target data for top candidates; choose the variant with maintained or enhanced on‑target activity (≥100 % WT) and the fewest off‑target sites.
For FrCas9, V1103K is the lead variant (30.15 % fidelity improvement) over V1103R.

steps.title: Sequence alignment of PLL regions
steps.instruction: Retrieve target Cas9 sequences and align them with FrCas9 to locate the PLL motif for engineering.

substeps.instruction: Download the target Cas9 protein sequence (e.g., EvCas9, GsCas9) from UniProt or NCBI.
Align the target sequence with FrCas9 using Clustal Omega or MUSCLE (default settings).
Identify the PLL motif corresponding to FrCas9 D1101‑S1102‑V1103 and note the analogous residue number and native amino acid in the target Cas9.

steps.title: Structural assessment and validation
steps.instruction: Obtain or predict the Cas9‑sgRNA‑DNA structure and verify its quality before PLL analysis.

substeps.instruction: Download an experimental crystal structure from the PDB if available; otherwise generate an AlphaFold3 prediction of the Cas9‑sgRNA‑DNA ternary complex.
Validate the model: check the predicted alignment error (PAE) plot and ensure errors are ≤5 Å in the DNA‑binding region.
Upload the structure to the PISA server to analyze protein‑DNA interfaces and identify residues forming hydrogen bonds or salt bridges with the +1 phosphate.
Confirm that the PLL loop and surrounding residues are correctly modeled; note that high PAE in the non‑target strand may render the model unsuitable.

steps.title: Select candidate positions and design mutations
steps.instruction: Identify PLL positions analogous to FrCas9 V1103 in other orthologs and design rational K/R substitutions.

substeps.instruction: Using structural alignment, locate the analogous positions: EvCas9 N1102 and GsCas9 T1106.

Verify each candidate meets the criteria: within the PLL loop (3‑5 residues), 5‑8 Å from the +1 phosphate, flanked by residues that make stronger contacts (like FrCas9 D1101/S1102), and cavity volume >50 Å³ (CASTp analysis).
Design mutations: EvCas9 N1102 → R (N1102R) and GsCas9 T1106 → R (T1106R), based on the principle that long, positively charged side chains improve phosphate interaction.
Record the rationale: positive charge and side‑chain length are expected to enhance fidelity without steric clash.

steps.title: Visualize mutations in ChimeraX
steps.instruction: Model the proposed mutations and evaluate steric and electrostatic compatibility.

substeps.instruction: Load the candidate structures (EvCas9 N1102, GsCas9 T1106) into ChimeraX.
Display the target residue and surrounding atoms within a 5 Å sphere; show the DNA backbone as a surface.
Use the Mutagenesis Wizard to replace the native residue with arginine (or lysine if needed) and rotate the view to inspect for van‑der‑Waals overlaps.
Color residues by charge (blue = positive, red = negative, white = neutral) and assess the local electrostatic environment.
Measure the distance from the modeled side‑chain terminal nitrogen to the nearest phosphate oxygen; distances ≤8 Å are considered favorable.
Compare the modeled orientation to the FrCas9 V1103K structure to ensure similar phosphate‑targeting geometry.

steps.title: Finalize mutation design rationale
steps.instruction: Document the design decisions and plan experimental validation based on structural inspection.

substeps.instruction: Record the design rationale for each mutation (e.g., EvCas9‑N1102R: clear cavity, favorable geometry, analogous to FrCas9 V1103K).
If no severe steric clashes are observed, proceed to experimental validation (Phase 3).
If clashes are detected, consider alternative substitutions (K instead of R, or neutral polar residues Q/N) and repeat visual assessment.
Predict experimental outcomes: ≥100 % activity relative to wild‑type and maintained or improved specificity, based on FrCas9 V1103K data.

description: In the following protocol, we describe a structure-guided approach to engineer the phosphate-locking loop (PLL) domain in CRISPR-Cas9 nucleases for enhanced editing fidelity. Using FrCas9 as a model system, cryo-EM structural analysis identified an electron density cavity at residue V1103 within the D1101-S1102-V1103 PLL motif. Detailed structural characterization revealed that D1101 and S1102 form multiple hydrogen bonds and salt bridges with the +1 phosphate of the target DNA strand, while. V1103 contributes minimal direct contact—presenting an engineering-amenable cavity suitable for introducing beneficial interactions. We performed comprehensive mutagenesis at FrCas9 V1103, testing all 19 amino acid substitutions to systematically map structure-activity relationships. This revealed that extended, positively charged residues (K, R) optimally enhance both phosphate backbone interactions and editing fidelity, with V1103K achieving 30.15% improvement across nine target sites. Structural analysis of successful and unsuccessful variants established key design principles: optimal substitutions introduce favorable electrostatic interactions while maintaining appropriate spatial geometry within the cavity, whereas aromatic residues cause steric clashes and negatively charged residues disrupt DNA binding through electrostatic repulsion. These structure-activity insights, derived from FrCas9 characterization, inform rational engineering of analogous PLL positions in other Cas9 systems. The protocol integrates structural analysis of protein-DNA interfaces—including hydrogen bonding patterns, salt bridge formation, cavity geometry, and electrostatic complementarity—with functional validation through genome editing assays and high-throughput sequencing. This approach has been successfully applied to EvCas9 and GsCas9, demonstrating broad applicability across Type II-A Cas9 orthologs with conserved PLL architecture.2,3,4,5,6
